<p class="foot"><b>Counted:</b> Kotlin, JavaScript, HTML, Swift, Python, Rust, C/C++/Objective-C, Go and shader source (GLSL, Slang, Metal, HLSL), all lines including blanks and comments. Swift is the visionOS head and its encoder; Rust is the paint engine's Field-side code (<code>native/field-paint/src</code> and the <code>src/field/</code> it adds to the forked crate); C/C++ is the native helpers under <code>native/</code>. Python is Field4's <code>tools/</code> plus the <code>field-audio-ai</code> service. <b>Starting points &amp; lessons</b> is the box code saved in documents &mdash; the welcome page's starting points, the graphics lessons, the agent and docs demo documents &mdash; with identical copies counted once. <b>Excluded as vendored</b> (316,358 lines today): the Monaco editor, the three.js editor and its <code>examples/</code> trees, A-Frame, super-three, CodeMirror and its modes, acorn/tern, tess2, every <code>.min.js</code>, the forked claude-paint crate, FFmpeg's NVENC headers and Steam Audio's C API. <b>Excluded as generated</b> (21,705 lines): <code>src/generatedLinalg/</code>, the RectSL/StackSL gallery wrappers, and saved <code>templates/</code> sheets. <b>Docs</b> are the contents pages' Markdown, skipping any page whose first line says a generator wrote it. <b>Method:</b> one point per day, taken from the largest tree committed that day, so the line follows the leading edge where branches ran in parallel. The submodule is counted through the gitlink Field4 pins, so it appears the day Field4 adopted it. The visionOS app's original commit root is left out (its Swift is counted from the main line). Kotlin is ~80% of the total, so the small bands are only a few pixels tall &mdash; read their values from the legend, the tooltip or the table. Generated by <code>tools/loc_chart.py</code>.</p>
</div>
<script>
(function(){
const root = document.currentScript.previousElementSibling;
const L=56, R=838;
const fmt = v => v.toLocaleString('en-US');
const css = k => getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue(k).trim();
// rows are [date, v1..vn]; bands are {name, v} drawn stacked when `stacked`, else as lines.
// `extra(row)` returns [label, value] rows shown under the bands, `total` adds a Total row.
function wire(name, rows, bands, opts){
  const wrap = root.querySelector('[data-chart="' + name + '"]');
  const svg = wrap.querySelector('svg'), tip = wrap.querySelector('.tip');
  const hit = svg.querySelector('.hit'), cross = svg.querySelector('.cross');
  const dots = [...svg.querySelectorAll('.dot')];
  const n = rows.length, H = opts.height;
  const px = i => L + (R-L)*i/(n-1);
  const py = v => opts.bottom - (opts.bottom-opts.top)*v/opts.ymax;
  function row(label, value, colour){
    const r = document.createElement('div'); r.className = 'r';
    if (colour){
      const key = document.createElement('i'); key.className = 'k';
      key.style.background = colour; r.appendChild(key);
    }
    // Series names are data — textContent, never innerHTML.
    const nm = document.createElement('span'); nm.className = 'n';
    nm.textContent = label; r.appendChild(nm);
    const val = document.createElement('span'); val.className = 'v';
    val.textContent = fmt(value); r.appendChild(val);
    return r;
  }
  function show(e){
    const r = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
    const x = (e.clientX - r.left) / r.width * 960;
    const i = Math.max(0, Math.min(n-1, Math.round((x - L)/(R-L)*(n-1))));
    const d = rows[i], vx = px(i);
    cross.setAttribute('x1', vx); cross.setAttribute('x2', vx);
    cross.style.opacity = 1;
    let acc = 0, top = 0;

## Scope

This catalog covers the JVM Kotlin source tree. Shared protocol and browser source sets, private personal code and generated vector algebra are separate from that inventory. The generated `afield.math.linalg` API has its own [reference](../linear_algebra_api.md), with [Linear algebra in Field](../linear_algebra.md) for the intuition.

## How to read a symbol you find here

Type its name in a box and press `ctrl-space`: the [completion documentation panel](../completion_doc_browser.md) shows the same KDoc with every resolvable `[Symbol]` reference turned into a link you can follow, plus a jump straight to the definition's line in the source. This reference and that panel read declarations through the same parser. Entries marked internal here may be hidden from autocomplete; use their source links to inspect the implementation.

To search rather than browse, see [The Semantic Index](../semantic_index.md).
